To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the ice particle pore structure is not only a function of growth mode and growth conditions but also of the ice particle size.

the pore structure of rimed particles, in particular graupel, can be imaged by synchrotronic micro-tomography at μm spatial scale in the original state and that this technique can be applied for studying the pore structure of natural ice particles in the atmosphere.

(1) the pore structure of graupel is characterized by Y-shaped voids with a mean diameter of 10-20 μm, which are not present in annealed particles; (2) the pore structure is not homogeneously distributed within the graupel grain, but is rather concentrated in a few large pores; and (3) the pore structure can be used to distinguish between different growth modes.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of a new experimental approach for the investigation of the pore structure of ice particles by means of synchrotron X-ray micro-tomography and its application on naturally rimed ice particles.
the development of the experimental methods and the application of these methods in the study of ice particle growth in mixed-phase and supercooled clouds.
the development of a novel cryo-stage for the synchrotron X-ray micro-tomography setup to image the 3-D pore structure of ice particles.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Y-shaped pore structure is not a typical structure for graupel particles, but rather an artificial structure resulting from a thermal annealing of the sample.
the Y-shaped pore morphology is a typical feature of in situ grown graupel particles and is not a result of annealing.
the Y-shaped pore morphology is a characteristic feature of the in situ structure of natural graupel particles.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the pore structure in graupel grains is highly complex, and the ice particle growth history is reflected in the bubble distribution and size.
the pore structure in rimed graupels can be regarded as an important fingerprint for the growth mode and the growth history of the particle.
the new cryo-stage setup for synchrotron X-ray tomography provides a unique possibility to study the in situ pore morphology of individual rimed ice particles at the μm resolution scale.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Kelvin effect can be avoided by using synchrotron radiation micro-tomography at 77 K.
the pore morphology of rimed particles is not necessarily a result of a growth process but may also be a result of a post-growth process, e.g., due to the Kelvin-effect.
it is not possible to derive the in situ bubble structure at sub-mm scale by annealing at 265 K.
